transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time with how my face looks. It sounds a bit silly saying it out loud, but I keep noticing this drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw—especially in photos or reflections.

Other people tell me I look fine, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but to me it feels really obvious. It’s started affecting work too… I’ve been avoiding presentations and meeting with clients when I can. I know that probably sounds excessive, but it’s been hard to get past.
How much time during the day would you say you spend thinking about or worrying about how your face looks?

I mean… probably more than I’d like to admit. It’s not like I sit down and plan to think about it, but every time I see a reflection or a photo, I notice the droop around my mouth and jaw, and then I sort of get stuck on it.

I try to tell myself other people say I look fine, so maybe I’m overreacting, but it feels really obvious to me. It’s enough that it keeps coming back during the day, especially if I know I have to be seen by people. Does that make sense?
Have you ever felt so distressed about how your face looks that it significantly interferes with your daily life, like avoiding social situations or work responsibilities?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but… yes, it has interfered.

I cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute because I just couldn’t make myself stand in front of everyone looking like this. And there have been these award-related networking events I was supposed to go to, which would be good for my work, but I’ve been missing them because I can’t face being seen.

It’s embarrassing to admit, but my project deadlines have started slipping, and even family gatherings are getting harder to manage. I know that probably sounds unreasonable… but it feels like things are starting to fall apart around it.

When you look at your face and see the drooping or unevenness around your mouth and jaw, do you believe that this is something that others can clearly notice, or do you feel like they might not see it unless you point it out?

I… I know people tell me they don’t really see it, or that I look fine, and I try to believe them. But when I look in a mirror or see a photo, it feels so obvious to me—like the drooping around my mouth and jaw is right there.

So I guess part of me thinks other people must notice it too, even if they’re being polite and not saying anything. Maybe that sounds unfair to them, but it’s hard for me to shake.

When you worry about your face looking uneven or droopy, do you feel like this is something that is clearly visible to others and should be noticeable, or do you think it might be something only you can really see or feel?

I guess… I know the “right” answer is probably that other people may not see it the way I do. And people do tell me I look fine.

But to me, it feels clearly visible. Like in every photo or reflection, my eye goes straight to the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw, and it feels like it must be noticeable to anyone looking at me. I’m trying not to overstate it, but it’s gotten to where I avoid presentations or clients because I’m so sure they’ll see it. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had medical or dermatological evaluations to check if there is an underlying physical cause for the drooping or unevenness you see around your mouth and jaw?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly… I mean, I haven’t really had a clear explanation for it, if that’s what you mean.

I don’t want to assume it’s medical if it isn’t, but I also don’t know that anyone has definitively checked it in a way that would settle it for me. Does that make sense?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical or neurological condition that affects the muscles or appearance of your face, such as Bell’s palsy or facial nerve palsy?

No… not that I know of. I’ve never been told I had Bell’s palsy or anything like facial nerve palsy.

I mean, I don’t want to say that too confidently if there’s something I missed, but no doctor has diagnosed me with something like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Would you say that the unevenness or drooping you see around your mouth and jaw is something you believe should be noticeable to others, or is it more of a subtle thing that only you seem to focus on?

I think… I know people say it’s probably subtle, and I’m trying to accept that, but honestly it feels like it should be noticeable to others.

I can’t stop seeing the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw in photos and reflections. My eyes go right to it every time. Even when people tell me I look fine, it just feels so obvious to me that I’ve started avoiding presentations and clients because I’m worried they’ll see it too. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you ever had a medical evaluation specifically to rule out a neurological or muscular condition causing the facial asymmetry you're describing?

I don’t think I’ve had anything that specific, no. I mean, I’ve seen doctors before in general, but I don’t remember anyone doing a focused neurological or muscle evaluation for my face to rule that out.

I don’t want to overstate it—I may not know exactly what would count as that kind of evaluation. But no one has sat me down and said, “We’ve ruled out a nerve or muscle issue.” Is that what you’re asking?
Would you say that the drooping and unevenness around your mouth and jaw is something that you believe is clearly visible and significant, even if others don’t seem to notice it?

Yes… I guess I would say that. I know other people don’t always seem to notice it, or they tell me I look fine, but to me it feels very clear.

In photos or even just reflections, I go straight to the drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. I’m trying not to make too much of it, but it feels significant enough that I’ve started avoiding presentations and meeting with clients sometimes, because I’m afraid they’ll see what I see. Does that make sense?

When you worry about how your face looks, is it mainly the appearance of the drooping and unevenness around your mouth and jaw that bothers you, or is it more about how others might react to it or judge you because of it?

I think it starts with the appearance itself… the drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. That’s what I can’t seem to stop seeing, especially in photos or reflections.

But then it turns into worrying that other people will notice it too, or judge me for it. I know people tell me I look fine, and maybe I’m being too focused on it, but it feels obvious to me. Obvious enough that I’ve avoided presentations and clients sometimes, which I’m embarrassed to admit. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever felt so consumed by the idea that your face looks uneven or droopy that it’s hard to focus on anything else, even for a period of time?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there are times when I just can’t stop seeing it—the droop and the unevenness around my mouth and jaw.

Like if I catch myself in a reflection or see a photo, my mind goes right there, and then it’s hard to concentrate on what I’m supposed to be doing. Even when people tell me I look fine, it still feels really obvious to me. It’s gotten to the point where I’ve avoided presentations or meeting with clients because I’m afraid I won’t be able to stop thinking about it, or that they’ll notice too.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of “consumed” you mean, but… yes, I think that’s fair to say.

When you worry about the drooping or unevenness around your mouth and jaw, do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors repeatedly, taking lots of photos, or trying to cover your face to make sure it looks okay?

Yes… I do some of that. Probably more than I’d like to admit.

Before work, or if we’re going to a family event, I can get stuck in the bathroom for a long time checking the mirror. I’ll take pictures on my phone from different angles to see if it looks as bad as I think it does, and then I’ll redo my makeup or adjust a scarf to try to make it look less noticeable.

I also ask my husband if my face looks lopsided… sometimes more than once, which I know probably isn’t fair to him. And then, this is embarrassing, but I’ll sometimes scroll through photos of other women and compare my face to theirs, just to see how bad mine looks next to them.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to be difficult; I just feel like I need to check before I can go out.

Would you say that the way your face looks—specifically the drooping and unevenness around your mouth and jaw—is something that you believe is clearly visible and looks abnormal to others, even though most people probably wouldn’t notice it or think it looks bad?

Yes… I think that’s right. I know other people probably don’t see it the way I do, or at least they tell me they don’t. But to me it looks very obvious, like the droop around my mouth and jaw is the first thing you’d notice.

I feel a little embarrassed saying that, because I understand it may not look “abnormal” to everyone else. But in photos or reflections, I can’t stop seeing it. It feels so visible that I’ve avoided presentations and clients because I’m afraid they’ll notice it too. Does that make sense?
